column11: ANCHOR, a measured analogue: the PCSK9 inhibitors, the last high-priced injectable lipid class to launch into a prevalent US pool against payer prior authorisation. In one large US cardiology practice, Cardiology Consultants of Philadelphia with 97 cardiologists (Smith A et al., J Clin Med 2021;10:3828, doi:10.3390/jcm10173828, PMC8432238, Table 2) the yearly share of eligible ASCVD patients newly prescribed one was 0.26% in 2015 (from the July launch), 1.23% in 2016, 1.09% in 2017, 1.52% in 2018 and 1.60% in 2019: 45, 216, 196, 286 and 316 patients over 17,267 to 19,689 eligible. That is the engine's penetration itself, new starts over eligible patients, so it is fitted directly: a logistic with peak 0.0142, k 3.06 and midpoint -0.55 years from the first full year (2016) fits the five years to an rmse of 0.17 points, 2015 taken at year -1 as measured and not annualised. MULTIPLE 0.25, A JUDGEMENT: 0.25 x 0.0142 = 0.00355. The case: that rate was a whole class with two drugs; solbinsiran would be the third RNA drug into sHTG after olezarsen (approved June 2026) and plozasiran, both APOC3, which cut triglycerides by about 80% in sHTG (SHASTA-3 and SHASTA-4 medians of 79% and 81%, Arrowhead 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-06-30) against solbinsiran's 58% to 60% in mixed dyslipidaemia (NCT05256654), and olezarsen and plozasiran report fewer pancreatitis events where solbinsiran has no such data. For it: ANGPTL3 silencing also lowered apoB in PROLONG-ANG3 (24.3% at 400 mg against 11.6% on placebo at day 180), a second lipid benefit
column12: the 0.25 multiple is the most arguable figure here. The PCSK9 rates were lifted by the FOURIER outcomes trial (presented March 2017) and the March 2018 price cut. The paper's abstract gives 0.5% to 3.3%, which are the table's new prescriptions per physician, not per eligible patient; the table's per-patient rates are used. The eligible patients were ASCVD patients with LDL-C of 70 or more seen by cardiologists that year, a specialist setting where new drugs start faster than in the primary care most sHTG patients see, so the anchor leans high
